subject: [PATCH 3/3] perf/core: Don't zero perf_sample_data in do_perf_sw_event()

2026-11-19.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the performance of software events in the Linux kernel by preventing unnecessary zeroing of a struct perf_sample_data on function entry when CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO is enabled. The struct is marked as __uninitialized, which allows its contents to be copied into a ring buffer without being cleared first. This change reduces the time added to context switches from 54 ns to 44 ns in certain scenarios.

reviews.author: Peter Zijlstra
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch only partially addresses the issue of stack initialization and suggested making all instances consistent by folding in additional changes from a git-grep search.

reviews.author: Peter Zijlstra
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch only applies to kernel/events/core.c, but similar changes are needed in other files (arch/x86/events/*.c) and should be split into separate patches.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed Peter's concern about perf_tp_event(), perf_bp_event(), and perf_swevent_hrtimer() not initializing their sample data correctly, explaining that they do call perf_sample_data_init(). However, the author also mentioned that these functions need a separate fix from patch 2 to work.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks! I went through the below. perf_tp_event(), perf_bp_event()
and perf_swevent_hrtimer() call perf_sample_data_init() for each event,
like do_perf_sw_event() does. The side-band emitters only use the
sample ID fields, which perf_event_header__init() writes and
perf_event__output_id_sample() reads under the same sample_id_all
check. So they are all fine to do.

But they do need the fix in patch 2 to work.

There is another fix that I found looking at your next reply.
Would you like me to send all the fixes and you can then send
the below patch (and the next one?)

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the patch for PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT still had a bug and promised to fix it in a separate commit (e662f8539ca00096db3ee4d570efe97767427fbe) which writes var3_w as well. This suggests that the original patch will need further revision.
reviews.raw_body:
Agreed, but IBS is not safe yet. For PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT,
perf_ibs_parse_ld_st_data() writes only var1_dw and var2_w but sets
PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_TYPE, so perf_output_sample() copies var3_w from
whatever is on the stack. INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO hides that today, and
INIT_STACK_NONE kernels have leaked those 2 bytes since 6b2ae4952ef8.
With __uninitialized in perf_ibs_handle_irq() every kernel would.

We need the below:

commit e662f8539ca00096db3ee4d570efe97767427fbe
Author: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
Date:   Fri Nov 20 09:04:13 2026 -0800

    perf/x86/amd/ibs: Don't leak stack contents through PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT

    For a load that missed the data cache, perf_ibs_parse_ld_st_data()
    reports the miss latency as the sample weight and marks
    PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_TYPE as done, so perf_prepare_sample() leaves the
    field alone. With PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT it writes only var1_dw and
    var2_w, but perf_output_sample() copies all 8 bytes of the union into
    the ring buffer. var3_w therefore carries whatever was left in the
    on-stack struct perf_sample_data in perf_ibs_handle_irq().

    CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO hides this by clearing the struct on entry.
    Without it, every such sample hands 2 bytes of kernel stack to user
    space. "perf mem record" asks for PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT on x86, and
    since v6.14 swfilt lets an unprivileged user sample their own tasks with
    IBS.

    Write var3_w as well.

    Fixes: 6b2ae4952ef8 ("perf/x86/amd: Support PERF_SAMPLE_{WEIGHT|WEIGHT_STRUCT}")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c b/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c
index 66e67e27224f18..9aa47751b37f6c 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c
+++ b/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c
@@ -1376,6 +1376,7 @@ static void perf_ibs_parse_ld_st_data(__u64 sample_type,
                if (sample_type & PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT) {
                        data->weight.var1_dw = op_data3.dc_miss_lat;
                        data->weight.var2_w = op_data.tag_to_ret_ctr;
+                       data->weight.var3_w = 0;
                } else if (sample_type & PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT) {
                        data->weight.full = op_data3.dc_miss_lat;
                }


The other sites look fine to me, including arch-PEBS: the drain skips
records whose first fragment has no basic group, so var3_w is always
written there.

2026-11-20.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the performance of software events in Linux by avoiding unnecessary zeroing of a local variable in the do_perf_sw_event() function. The function is called on every context switch, which can be a significant overhead when running many small VMs. By marking the struct as __uninitialized, the contents are not cleared unnecessarily, reducing the time spent on software counters from 54 ns to 44 ns. This change is particularly beneficial for hosts with many small VMs and KVM guests on AMD Zen 5 CPUs.
